subject: phoenix
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module to build a phoenix with the SDK, going for a standing pose with wings partly raised, flame-like crest, and long tail feathers, scaled to roughly life-size proportions with the ground at y=0.

I'm defining a color palette of fiery reds, oranges, and golds for the body, beak, and claws, and sketching out a skeleton starting with hips as the root spine joint and a curved spine chain rising forward into the neck and body, aiming to keep the joint and limb setup simple enough to avoid runtime issues.

Building the skeleton hierarchy...

I'm defining the beak curve points off the head's local coordinates, then adding a jaw joint parented to the head so the lower beak can hinge, with eye spheres to follow.

Now I'm sketching out a flame-like crest made of several spiky bezier sweeps spread across the head and tipped in gold, then starting a wing chain structure from a shoulder joint through elbow and wrist to a feathered wingtip.

For feathers, I'm weighing options like extruded leaf shapes versus textured cards, and leaning toward extruded outlines placed along the wing bone points, oriented so the outline runs along the wing direction with the up vector handling the leaf curvature.

Working out the orientation math so the feather plane lies horizontal with thickness pointing vertically, letting feathers fan backward and stack naturally like a bird's wing.

I'm sketching a feather outline shape with points curving along the wing length and tapering back, then thinking about distributing feathers along the trailing edge using a chain-based placement so each one picks up the right position and orientation.

For the wings, I need mirrored geometry for left and right sides, flipping the x-direction so feather thickness stays consistent while allowing a slight dihedral lift. I'm defining the wing's curve in model space using a catmull-rom spline through shoulder, mid-wing, and tip points, positioned relative to the torso and shoulder joints.

For the chain naming, I'm working out that a wing path with four control points produces three spans, requiring four joint names (shoulder, elbow, wrist, tip) with the tip acting as the terminal joint. I'm deciding the wing chain should parent to the second spine joint, and reworking the spine path itself to use four points instead of fewer, giving it more segments and joints along the torso curve.

For the wings, I'm sweeping a tapered radius along the chain to create the bone shape, then placing feather rows using along() callbacks that leverage each ChainPoint's frame conversion so orientation and bone inheritance work automatically. I'm now thinking through how each feather's outline should be oriented outward and trailing along the wing's curve.

Planning primaries versus coverts as two feather rows with different lengths and counts, and designing a reusable feather outline function parameterized by length and width so I can scale it for each row. For coloring, I'm considering a paint function that gradients each feather from gold at the root to red at the tip based on position along the outline.

For the body, I'm sculpting a sweep profile along the spine so it's plump in the middle like a fattened belly, then thinking through how to apply a countershaded gold-to-red paint across the torso to match the phoenix color scheme.

For the head I'm using a simple low-poly sphere with flat shading for a stylized faceted look, positioned slightly forward and offset at the head bone. The neck gets its own tapered sweep in a warm orange.

For the tail, I'm laying out a catmull chain of bones sweeping down and back from the hips to the ground, tapering the thickness toward the tip, then planning to scatter feather extrusions along its length using `b.along`.

Working out the orientation math for those tail feathers now — I need the cross product of the extrude's along-direction and spread-direction vectors to get the right thickness plane, and I'm considering fanning the feathers outward with varying spread angles per index to get a natural feather-fan silhouette.

Now I'm working through leg placement: hip joint position, target foot position, and checking whether the limb segment lengths can actually reach that target given the distance involved. I realize my initial lengths fall short of the required reach, so I adjust the thigh, shin, and foot segment lengths to be longer, then think through the bend directions needed for a bird-like digitigrade leg structure.

I decide to reverse the knee/hock bend directions since birds flex differently than typical hind limbs, settling on knee pointing back and hock pointing forward. Then I start sketching out the leg chain definition with named joints for hip, knee, ankle, and foot, and begin planning how to attach toe segments extending forward from the foot tip joint.

Now I'm working out toe placement — small capsules fanning out from the foot tip at slight left/right offsets, checking that their radius keeps the lowest points within an acceptable sink tolerance relative to the leg target height, and I settle on lowering the foot target to ground level so the toes sink just slightly rather than hover.

I'm now sketching the limb chains themselves: legs built from hip socket to ground target using the limb helper returning a polyline of points for b.chain, with wings and tail as separate chain structures, plus thinking about a flame-colored tail accent. Roughly tallying joint and part counts for hips, spine, neck, head, legs, wings, and tail, then placing eye spheres on the head with forward/left/up offsets.

Now I'm defining the beak as a tapered sweep from the head joint, running from a wider base to a pointed tip with a slight downward curve, using rounded-to-point end caps. I'm also setting up the jaw joint, parented to the head, aimed slightly forward and down to form the mouth hinge.

I'm sketching the crest as a row of flame-like sweeps along the top of the head, spacing them outward with the center one colored differently to stand out like a flame among the gold spikes, then placing the head itself as a sphere attached to the head bone.

Now I'm defining a reusable feather helper that builds leaf-shaped outlines from a length and width, with sharp corners at the tip and curved edges along the sides, so I can reuse it for body plumage and the neck sweep.

For wing placement I'm working out orientation: making the feather's cross-axis align with depth so the leaf fans outward correctly, tilting each feather slightly backward along the chain direction, and mirroring the rotation vectors for the opposite wing so both sides fan symmetrically.

I realize the feathers are overlapping too densely near the tip since the sampling spacing is smaller than each leaf's length, so I'm adjusting the direction vectors to angle primaries backward and outward like real trailing feathers rather than stacking forward along the wing bone.

Working out perpendicular direction vectors for feather orientation...

Setting up colors for tail feathers gradient from gold to flame, leg sweep radii in orange-gold, and torso countershading between flame and gold tones along the spine path with varying radius for the hips.

I'm laying out the skeleton: a four-point spine chain extending into a neck and head, with wings rooted at a spine joint spreading into a long catmull curve for that phoenix-like span, and legs attached via hip sockets with target foot positions mirrored left and right.

Checking the leg joint chain — hip, knee, ankle, foot — lines up with four points from three bone lengths, and I'm working out toe placement as small capsules branching off the foot tip relative to its local frame.

I'm planning symmetric left/right leg construction with a shared sweep function and side-suffixed joint names, then setting feather row counts for primaries, coverts, and tail before starting to write the actual import statements and setup code.

Setting up color constants and imports...

Now I'm defining the feather outline shape and paint functions, then starting the skeleton build with hip and spine joints.

I'm sweeping the body profile with a radius function, realizing the sine formula creates a bad taper near the chest, so I'm reworking it into a piecewise linear function that widens through the belly and narrows toward the chest instead.

Now I'm defining the neck chain with its own taper, confirming it connects exactly at the spine's endpoint, then placing the head joint with an aim direction and attaching a flattened sphere offset slightly forward and up using the bone's local frame. I'm starting to set up the eyes next, looping over symmetric left/right positions.

For the eyes I'm computing the exact offsets so the eye spheres and pupils poke out slightly from the head sphere's surface rather than sinking in, checking the distances against the head radius and adjusting forward/left/up values until they sit correctly bulging outward.

Now I'm shaping the upper beak as a tapered sweep curve emerging from the head, making sure the base starts hidden inside the head sphere and the tip extends outward to a point.

Next I'm setting up a jaw joint attached to the head, aimed slightly forward and down, then sweeping a thinner lower beak curve from it so the beak looks subtly open with the lower tip sitting a bit below the upper tip.

Now I'm starting to build a crest out of a small loop of segments.

Writing crest sweep code...

Now I'm designing the wing chains, mirroring left and right using a sign multiplier, defining feather direction vectors that stay orthogonal, and sweeping the wing bones with a tapering radius and warm coloring.

Writing primary and covert feather code...

Next I'm building the tail chain off the hips with a curved path and tapering radius, then laying feathers along it using orthogonal direction vectors so they fan out horizontally, with color shifting toward flame near the tip.

Writing leg and foot code...

I'm placing toe capsules fanned out from each foot joint using local coordinates, then thinking through overall proportions to make sure the crest, head, and tail heights produce a plausible phoenix silhouette around 1.8 meters tall.

Writing body paint and export code...

I'm double-checking that all imports are actually used, finalizing capsule and sweep option signatures, confirming the paint function for primaries shifts color by position, and preparing to write the leaf helper function.

Defining the leaf outline shape...

The leaf shape forms a pointed almond with a sharp tip corner, and I'm deciding the tail feather coloring should flame out near the tip while coverts stay a simpler orange. Now I'm ready to assemble the full module.
